record.paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
record.original_question: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a non-trivial infinite-dimensional separable quotient?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. (Separable quotient problem) Does every infinite-dimensional Ba￾nach space have a non-trivial infinite-dimensional separable quotient?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space over the real or complex field. A quotient of X is a Banach space of the form X/M, where M is a closed linear subspace of X, equipped with the canonical quotient norm. Such a quotient is called non-trivial and infinite-dimensional separable if X/M is infinite-dimensional, separable (i.e., contains a countable dense subset), and not isomorphic to a finite-dimensional space.

Question: Must every infinite-dimensional Banach space X admit a closed subspace M ⊂ X such that the quotient X/M is infinite-dimensional and separable?
artifact.category_tag: Separable quotient problem for Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The separable quotient problem (Banach–Mazur, 1932) remains open in general. Affirmative answers are known in special cases such as reflexive spaces, weakly compactly generated spaces, and dual spaces, and recent works (e.g., 2017–2022) extend the class of Banach spaces for which the answer is known to be yes, but the general question is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Observations on the Separable Quotient Problem for Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The longstanding Banach–Mazur separable quotient problem asks whether every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a quotient that is both infinite-dimensional and separable. The centenary of this still open problem will be in 2032.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is still open as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: On the separable quotient problem for Banach spaces (arXiv:1709.09646)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys results on the separable quotient problem; affirmative for reflexive, WCG and dual spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results known but general problem unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting Mazur separable quotient problem (1932)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2022) revisit of the Mazur separable quotient problem.
status_evidence.claim: Problem continues to be actively studied and remains open.
